subject: Inventory request: third-party dependencies for async batching & KV cache paths
messages:
From: Alicia Wang <security@eduplatform.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: third-party dependency inventory for async batching paths

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

EduPlatform's security team is validating our vendor risk posture for a pilot that will stream inference requests through an external batching layer. Can you please provide a consolidated inventory of all third-party software and vendor services that touch the async batching and KV cache paths used by Redwood's hosted inference endpoints?

Specifically we need:
- A flat list of vendors and OSS libraries used in (a) request queuing/batching service, (b) KV cache persistence and replication, and (c) any ephemeral key brokers or tokenizers used at request time.
- The role of each dependency (network exposure, data residency, sensitive key access).
- Current assurance artifacts you can share (SOC 2, SIG, CAIQ, SBOM).

Deadline: 2026-05-25 EOD PT if possible — we have a compliance gate for the pilot.

Thanks,
Alicia Wang
Security Program Manager
EduPlatform Inc.

[attachment: pilot-scope-eduplatform.pdf]

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Alicia Wang <security@eduplatform.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 10:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: third-party dependency inventory for async batching paths

Alicia — thanks for the clear scope. I'm looping in Marissa and Ben to cover procurement and infra-side evidence. High level answers below; attaching a CSV with a first-pass inventory and our current SBOM export.

Quick summary (full CSV attached):
- Vendors: EdgeBatcher LLC (batching layer), CloudKV Inc. (optional remote KV replica), ephemeral-key service: TokenForge (used for short-lived ingestion tokens in dedicated deployments).
- OSS libs of note: fast-async-queue v1.4.2 (queueing), grpcio v1.48 (transport), lru-kv v0.9 (local cache), zstd compression lib v1.5.2.
- Exposure: EdgeBatcher is deployed in customer-dedicated VPCs for Dedicated customers; for hosted API we route to a Redwood-managed EdgeBatcher cluster in our US region with strict egress rules and no persistent student-identifiable data retained in the batching layer (we only persist request prefix hashes for rate limiting).

Requested artifacts attached: async-batching-deps-2026-05-19.csv, sbom-async-batcher-v2.json. For vendor evidence we have EdgeBatcher SOC 2 Type II in progress (expected Q3 2026); we can share current MSA and our redline. CloudKV has self-attested SIG-A responses which I'll summarize in a follow-up.

Questions for you:
1) Do you need us to separate OSS dependencies by version per deployment (hosted vs dedicated)?
2) Are there any specific CAIQ sections EduPlatform wants filled (network segmentation / cryptography / ephemeral keys)?

I'll follow up with a procurement note and the MSA redline.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Trust & Safety Engineer
Redwood Inference

[attachment: async-batching-deps-2026-05-19.csv]
[attachment: sbom-async-batcher-v2.json]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Alicia Wang <security@eduplatform.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: EdgeBatcher MSA + procurement note

Alicia — quick procurement context: EdgeBatcher LLC is our preferred vendor for the batching layer when customers opt into managed batching. We have a standing MSA (signed by some pilot customers) but we need to provide a version that includes the following for EduPlatform:
- Data residency clause (US-only processing for this pilot)
- Clarified deletion SLA for transient request artifacts (24 hours maximum; currently 48 default)
- Right-to-audit clause limited to a scoped SOC/attestation review (we can accept redacted evidence)

I've attached a redline of the MSA and an initial DocuSign link for a pilot amendment. If EduPlatform needs proof of SOC 2 earlier, we can offer additional compensating controls:
- Network egress allowlist between EduPlatform IPs and the EdgeBatcher instance
- Customer-side encryption for prefix hashes (we can provide a CEK pattern)

Marissa Cole
Senior Director, Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference

[attachment: edgebatcher-msa-redlined-2026-05-20.pdf]
[DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/link/ABC123-edgebatcher-msa]

From: ben_carter@redwood.com

Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 11:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Inventory request: third-party dependencies for async batching & KV cache paths

Adding a quick ops note: the cloudKV replica we sometimes enable for cross-region failover requires a service account with limited write permissions and uses a short-lived signed token (rotated every 12 hours). I'll attach a minimal access diagram to the internal doc. Also pushing for us to include the SBOM for the modified fast-async-queue (we vendor-patched one function for backpressure).

Ben Carter
Infrastructure Product Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A few follow-ups:
1) Please surface CloudKV's SIG-A PDF and the patched fast-async-queue SBOM sections where you changed the backpressure function.
2) For the MSA redline thanks — EduPlatform legal will review the DocuSign pilot amendment and come back with comments. If possible, please add the CAIQ network segmentation answers (we'll attach our custom CAIQ checklist).
3) Do you provide a timeline for the vendor SOC 2 Type II report? If Q3 is the earliest, we may require interim compensating controls (locks on egress, documented encryption-in-transit).

If you can send the CloudKV SIG and the patched SBOM by EOD Monday (2026-05-24) that should keep us on schedule.

Appreciate the quick turnaround,
Alicia

EduPlatform Inc.
